utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning. May I ask the Registrar to call out the name and number of the case?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case IT-95-16, the Prosecutor of the Tribunal against Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Vladimir Santic, also known as "Vlado", Drago Josipovic and Dragan Papic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I please have the appearances for the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, good morning, your Honours. My name is Mark Harmon, I will be representing the Prosecutor this morning and I will be assisted by my colleagues, Terree Bowers, who is seated to my right and Mr. Michael Blaxill, who is seated to my left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel for the accused, please introduce yourself and spell out your name clearly. Would you also indicate which bar you belong to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Your Honours, my name is Borislav Krajina, an attorney from Sarajevo, a member of the bar of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I am Defence counsel for the accused, Vlatko Kupreskic. With me is my learned colleague Zelimir Par, an attorney from Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we begin, I would like to check whether the accused can hear me in a language which is accessible to him. May I ask the accused whether he can follow, can understand what I am saying?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Your Honours, I understand you very well and hear you perfectly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. We now can commence this hearing. As you know, this is the initial appearance of the accused before the International Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, and the hearing is being held in accordance with the Statute of our Tribunal, as well as the Rules of Procedure and Evidence to formally charge the accused. As you know, these proceedings are being recorded and will be available to the public. Rule 62 of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence requires that an accused, after having his indictment confirmed by a Judge of this Tribunal, and after having been arrested and surrendered to the custody of the International Tribunal, must be formally charged at a procedure described as the initial appearance. Due to injuries sustained by the accused in the course of resisting arrest by SFOR troops, this initial appearance has had to be delayed until the accused was deemed to be medically fit to appear before this International Tribunal. We have now been informed that the accused is fit to enter his pleas to the charges brought against him by the Prosecutor. I would like now to ask the accused to rise and state for the Trial Chamber his name, date and place of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Your Honours, my name is Vlatko Kupreskic, I was born on 1st January 1958 in Pirici, Vitez municipality, the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You know that the rules governing our proceedings today are laid down in Articles 20 and 21 of the Statute of our Tribunal, and mention should also be made of Rule 62. I think you are all familiar with these provisions, so I will not try to summarise them for you, but we will proceed in accordance with the aforementioned provisions. May I now ask the Defence counsel whether he and his client have received copies of the indictment in a language which they understand, and whether the contents of the indictment were understood? Have you had adequate time to confer with your client in preparation for this initial appearance? This is a question I am asking you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have received the indictment and understood everything it contains. We have had sufficient time to confer with our client, so that we are quite prepared for today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. The indictment was issued by the Prosecutor on 2nd November 1995, and as you knew, was confirmed by Judge McDonald on 10th November 1995. Five of the persons indicted along with the accused are already in the custody of the International Tribunal, and have made their initial appearances accordingly. Charges against Marinko Katava and Stipo Alilovic have been withdrawn by the Prosecutor and therefore all references to them will be omitted in the indictment. In principle, under our Statute and our Rules of Procedure and Evidence, the entire indictment should be read out in court. May I ask whether the accused is prepared to waive this right to a public reading of the indictment? May I ask you, Defence counsel, whether the accused is prepared to waive his right to the reading out in court of the indictment, or would you like the indictment to be read out? Of course we would read out the relevant parts, the portions of the indictment which relate to the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have agreed that there is no need to read the indictment in its entirety, but if there is a short version, then we would be in favour of that shorter version being read out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I would say there is not a short version, but we could read out only those portions of the indictment which deal with the accused. We would skip the parts of the indictment which concern the other accused who have already come here for the initial appearance. Do you want those portions to be read out in court?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: No, your Honours, we feel that will not be necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. We can therefore now move on and I would like to turn to the accused. May I ask you to rise, Mr. Kupreskic. Could you stand up? Your counsel has informed the Trial Chamber that you have received a copy of the indictment in a language which you understand and that you comprehend the contents of the indictment. Please could you confirm whether this is correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have understood clearly the allegations in the indictment. However, it is not clear to me why my name is linked to that indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: This is a question which we could not answer. Your name, I assume, is linked to that indictment because according to the Prosecutor you must be charged with some crimes which are set out in the indictment. I would like therefore to move on and to recall each of the charges against you which are, as I say, set out in the indictment. Could you please tell the Trial Chamber whether you plead guilty or not guilty after I have put each count to you. The form of words we wish you to use is either "I plead guilty" or "I plead not guilty". Have you understood all this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So I will start with count 1. It is alleged that you individually, and in concert with Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vladimir Santic, Drago Josipovic and Dragan Papic participated in the unlawful and wanton destruction of property not justified by military necessity, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(d) of the Tribunal Statute. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I absolutely did not participate and I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 2. It is alleged that you individually, and in concert with Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vladimir Santic, Drago Josipovic and Dragan Papic, participated in the deliberate attack on the civilian population and wanton destruction of a village, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Tribunal Statute. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I did not participate, nor did I do those things, and I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 9. It is alleged that you participated in the wilful killing of Fata Pezer, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(a) of the Tribunal Statute. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I neither had occasion to do something like that, nor the opportunity to do it, nor the courage, nor the interest. I am absolutely not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right, you plead not guilty. Count 10. It is alleged that you participated in the wilful killing of Fata Pezer, a violation of the laws or customs of war, recognised by Article 3 of the Tribunal Statute. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I am absolutely not guilty because I am not capable of doing such a thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Not guilty. Count 11. It is alleged that you participated in wilfully causing Dzenana Pezer and a Bosnian Muslim civilian great suffering or serious injury to body or health, a grave breach recognised by Article 2(c) of the Tribunal Statute. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: My life and my authority would not allow this, I did not do that and I am absolutely not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Count 12. It is alleged that you participated in wilfully causing Dzenana Pezer and a Bosnian Muslim civilian great suffering or serious injury to body or health, a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Tribunal Statute. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: I plead absolutely not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may now be seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUPRESKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: You will be remanded now to the further custody of the International Tribunal and kept in the detention unit until further order is made. Would the Registrar please note the pleas of the accused. As the accused has pleaded not guilty to the charges against him, it is necessary for us to consider the organisation of the work of the Trial Chamber and the setting of a date for the trial. I wonder whether the Registrar is able to set a date for the trial now? May I ask the Registrar whether --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, I am not capable for the moment to give you the date for the beginning of trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. We shall then have to wait for confirmation from the Registry or suggestion from the Registry. I would like to remind now the Prosecutor of his obligation under Rule 66bis of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence, to make available to the Defence within 30 days of this initial appearance copies of the supporting material which accompanied the indictment when confirmation was sought, and also all prior statements obtained by the Office of the Prosecutor from the accused. Also, the Prosecutor is obliged to make available, no later than 60 days before the date set for trial, copies of the statements of all witnesses whom the Prosecutor intends to call to testify at trial. The statements of any additional witnesses shall be made available as soon as a decision is made to call those witnesses. Further orders may be made by the Trial Chamber in the interests of a fair and expeditious trial for the accused. Could I therefore ask if any such documents have already been provided to the Defence? If not, could I ask if the Prosecutor could indicate a time-frame within which these materials can be provided to Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President and your Honours, prior to the commencement of this proceeding, I provided counsel with copies of all supporting materials that accompanied the indictment in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. So Mr. Krajina, do you understand what the Prosecutor has just said? You have been entitled and you have received all the documents that were attached to the indictment, and to the request for information. Now I wish to remind the parties that under Rule 72 of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence, they have 60 days from the date of disclosure by the Prosecutor to the Defence of all material and statements provided under Rule 66bis (A), 60 days within which they must file any preliminary motions. Other motions, of course, may be filed under Rule 73. You are aware of this time limit, 60 days for filing preliminary motions. I wonder whether my colleagues have any further questions. No questions? As you know, it has been agreed that following this hearing, a closed session Status Conference will be held here, actually in half an hour, in order to look in greater detail at the state of preparedness of the parties for trial and also in order to settle any outstanding issues. If there are no comments or no suggestions or queries from either the Defence or the Prosecutor, I will now call an adjournment for 30 minutes, after which we shall reconvene in closed session to deal with this Status Conference. The hearing is adjourned. (9.20 am)
